title: Portland coffee shop
subtitle: Arabica after the Brazil frost, as of 15 Dec 2021
text: I run a coffee shop in Portland, Oregon, and sell about 2,500 drinks a week. An average drink sells for $4.25 and costs about $1.30 to make, of which the coffee is about a quarter. Our roaster delivers every two weeks and we keep about 3 weeks of coffee. The chain café nearby charges $4.50. I could put $5,000 into stock.

what_happened.text: The monthly arabica price peaked at its highest since 2011, after the 2021 frosts and dry weather in Brazil.
Frost worries in Brazil eased and arabica fell to a six-month low.
The World Bank's monthly arabica price was $5.64 a kg, against $5.91 in December 2021: within a few percent all along.

hindsight: Arabica stayed within a few percent of its December price all along, so the price rise and extra marketing were not needed.
caveats: Coffee is about a quarter of a drink's cost in the owner's own words (milk, cups and syrups are the rest). A café buys roasted coffee, which follows the green bean price with a lag.
The series is the world arabica green bean price (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/kg). It is a 'nothing much happened' case: prices were already high and stayed high.
Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them.
